problems.source_says: The paper presents group mean and subtracted networks but does not specify the observation or accumulation unit used to construct those means. The codebook defines unit as one observation in the paper's analysis, so a displayed group mean does not establish that one condition's whole pool of outputs was the analysis unit. The form itself acknowledges that the underlying ENA unit is unstated; set is therefore unsupported, and the unit should remain null pending clarification.
problems.quote: Figure 3 shows the post-test mean networks for both groups and the between-group differences reflected in the subtracted network.
problems.locator: PDF p. 12, Data analysis, ENA modeling paragraph; p. 13, Results RQ2; p. 14, Fig. 3. Codebook section 6, Unit.

problems.source_says: The inquiry analysis displays group mean networks and centroid trajectories across three topics. Neither the methods nor the figure identifies what constitutes an observation before those summaries are calculated. Group-level presentation alone cannot establish the codebook's set analysis unit; the actual unit is unreported and should remain null. No participant or output unit can be substituted with confidence from the supplied paper.
problems.quote: The mean networks and centroid trajectories across the inquiry topics (Fig. 4) further indicate that the post-intervention structural differences did not emerge abruptly at the post-test stage, but developed gradually during the inquiry process.
problems.locator: PDF p. 12, Data analysis, ENA modeling paragraph; p. 13, Results RQ2, final paragraph; p. 14, Fig. 4. Codebook section 6, Unit.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 through S1-O4 score questions students actually produced in open-ended tests. Two trained researchers coded the responses; these are not students' self-reports.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 8-9, Problem posing ability tests; pp. 10-11, coding rubric and scoring; p. 12, Data analysis.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 is a problem-posing composite, with maximum contributions of 3 for number, 2 for category, and 5 for cognitive quality, totaling 10. It is not a direct overall-creativity rating.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, scoring paragraph and Eqs. 1-4.

confirmed.statement: S1-O2 uses researcher-assigned Bloom cognitive-depth codes R=1, P=2, A=3, E=4, C=5, averaged over each student's valid questions. The rubric is not a separate originality rating.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Table 3, Quality rows; p. 11, opening paragraph and Eq. 4.

confirmed.statement: S1-O3 is fluency measured by a banded question count: L1 through L5 multiplied by 0.6, maximum 3. Declarative statements are excluded; the printed L4 and L5 thresholds overlap at 20, as the form notes.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Table 3, Number rows and table note; p. 11, Eq. 2.

confirmed.statement: S1-O4 is two-thirds of the mean category point value, not a count of distinct categories or a comparison across people. The form correctly retains the source inconsistency between IQ=0 in Table 3 and IQ=1 in the explanatory prose.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Table 3, Category rows; p. 11, Eq. 3 and its explanatory paragraph.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 through S1-O4 use participant-level scores and analyze 89 complete cases: 45 chatbot and 44 search-engine students.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, score calculation; p. 12, Data analysis; p. 13, Table 5 headers.

confirmed.locator: PDF p. 13, Table 5, corresponding row and group headers; adjusted-df footnote for Category and Total Score.

confirmed.locator: PDF p. 13, Table 5, corresponding row and group headers; adjusted-df footnote for Category and Total Score.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 through S1-O5 appropriately leave AI availability, question, and immediate/delayed timing null. The paper places the post-test after the inquiry phase but does not explicitly establish tool removal, availability during testing, or the interval after instruction.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6, Fig. 1 and implementation procedure; pp. 8-9, test administration. Codebook sections 1 and 6.

confirmed.statement: S1-O5 and S1-O6 derive ENA networks from researcher-coded question categories and cognitive levels. They are output-based code-co-occurrence analyses, not across-person similarity or diversity measures; the other construct is supported.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 12, Data analysis, ENA methods; p. 13, Results RQ2; p. 14, Figs. 3-4.

confirmed.statement: S1-O6 was produced during assigned-tool use, so ai_available_when_produced=yes, timing=immediate, and question=with_ai follow the codebook. No quantity coding or problem-posing ability scores were calculated for this inquiry phase.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 6, implementation procedure; p. 11, paragraph preceding inter-rater reliability; p. 12, classroom dialogue/search records. Codebook sections 1 and 6.

confirmed.statement: The qualitative reported descriptions for S1-O5 and S1-O6 match the Results and figures. The paper reports no inferential ENA contrast; neither group formed stable connections involving the creating node.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 13, Results RQ2; p. 14, Figs. 3-4; p. 17, Discussion RQ2.

confirmed.statement: No additional distinct output outcome was identified in the supplied 22-page document, read through the end of its references. Cognitive load and technology acceptance are questionnaires, while the supplemental baseline and within-group analyses concern the already listed scores and networks.
confirmed.locator: Markdown lines 1-817; PDF p. 12, questionnaire and analysis methods; p. 13, Results RQ1-RQ2; pp. 14-16, questionnaire results; pp. 19-22, supplementary notice and references.

confirmed.statement: Additional files 1 and 2 are external to the supplied PDF, which has no embedded attachments. Their contents could not be independently checked: no matching local supplement was found, and Python urllib requests to the DOI and Springer article both failed with WinError 10013.

summary: The ENA outcomes' set units are unsupported because the paper reports group mean networks without specifying the underlying analysis unit. Eligibility holds because researchers scored students' produced questions, and all four post-test numerical contrasts match Table 5.
